steps.name: QC, design validation, shallow-sample assessment
caveats: Salmon 'counts as delivered' are frequently length-corrected or TPM-rescaled — the integer check is the deciding evidence, not the file name.
The 12 x 2 metadata dimension may include the header row; reconcile row counts before trusting it.
With only 12 samples, MDS/PCA are descriptive, not a formal outlier test; report distances, do not apply automated outlier rejection.
A shallow library does not automatically mean a failed sample — the ~4x deficit is handled by the downstream sensitivity model, not by silent exclusion.
steps.context: Inputs: gene-level counts CSV (12,000 rows x 13 columns = gene ID column + 12 sample columns) and a sample table (12 rows x 2 columns: sample, condition). Design: 6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, Homo sapiens, skin. Known issue: sample_01 library size ~4x below the median. This step is the gate for everything downstream — it decides whether the values are raw counts or length-corrected, what the row IDs are, and how extreme sample_01 is.
steps.question: Is the 12,000 x 12 matrix genuine raw integer counts for a clean 6 (AD lesional) vs 6 (control) two-group design, what identifier space do the gene rows use, and what is the quantitative footprint of sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median?
constraints: Read the two input files exactly as delivered; verify that the 12 sample columns in the counts matrix all match metadata rows and that condition has exactly 6 samples per group. If the join fails (the metadata table is 12 x 2, so confirm whether a header row is included and whether all 12 samples are present), report the exact mismatch and stop — do not invent labels.

Determine integer-ness: compute the fraction of non-zero values that are not integer-valued. If >1% are non-integer, flag the matrix as length-corrected (TPM-like) rather than raw counts — DESeq2 on raw-count assumptions would be invalid and the DE step must take its fallback path.

Identify the row-name space: check whether gene rows look like Ensembl IDs (ENSG...) or HGNC symbols; report which, and how many map to a unique symbol via the human organism annotation database (org.Hs.eg.db).
Compute per-sample library size, fraction of zero genes, PCA (first 3 PCs) and class-scaled MDS of the distance matrix; annotate sample_01 and its distance to the centroid of its condition group.
Report sample_01's median-of-ratios size factor relative to the group.
Do not exclude, down-weight, or modify any sample in the outputs of this step; do not install any software; work only from the two input files and the organism annotation database.
steps.description: Produce a QC report: per-sample library sizes, fraction of zeros, the integer-ness verdict on the count matrix, the gene-row ID space (Ensembl vs HGNC symbol), a metadata-to-counts join report, PCA and sample-to-sample MDS with sample_01's position and distance to its group centroid annotated, and sample_01's DESeq2-style size factor (median-of-ratios) computed for information. sample_01 is NOT excluded here — its treatment is the sensitivity model in the DE step.
acceptance_criteria: A QC report/table exists containing: per-sample library sizes, zero fractions, size factor per sample (sample_01 flagged), fraction of non-integer values with an explicit raw-vs-length-corrected verdict, and the gene ID space with symbol mapping rate.
A PCA plot and an MDS plot both exist with all 12 samples labeled by condition and sample_01 explicitly annotated.
The metadata-to-counts join is verified 12/12 with 6 per condition, or a specific, quoted mismatch is reported as a blocker.
No sample is dropped or altered.

plan.title: AD vs control bulk RNA-seq DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are 12 human skin bulk RNA-seq samples (6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) as Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 x 13 CSV) plus a 2-column condition table. One known defect: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. The plan therefore (1) validates the matrix before any modeling — integer-ness of the 'counts' (Salmon output is often length-corrected, which would invalidate treating them as raw counts), ID space of gene rows, design integrity, and the quantitative footprint of sample_01 in PCA/MDS — keeping it in the primary 6v6 design since dropping a sample from a 6v6 study costs power and breaks balance; (2) runs DESeq2 (with apeglm LFC shrinkage) on the primary design plus a sensitivity model with sample_01 removed, and quantifies stability between the two so the shallow sample's effect on gene-level conclusions is explicit rather than assumed; (3) tests the full ranked gene list against the MSigDB human hallmark sets (the 'hallmark pathways' the question names, provisioned in this environment for Homo sapiens) with WikiPathways human as a secondary layer, on both the primary and sensitivity ranked lists. The three steps form a strict chain: nothing downstream runs until the matrix type and design are verified.
